front: Khái niệm 'Phrasal Verbs (Three-part phrasal verbs)' trong Unit 9: Career Paths được định nghĩa như thế nào?
back:
Combinations of Verb + Adverb + Preposition that act as a single semantic unit (e.g., look forward to, come up with, run out of, keep up with). They are inseparable and always take an object.

💡 Ví dụ: Young graduates must keep up with technological advancements in their profession.
🌱 Bản chất: Idiomatic authenticity in natural spoken and written English discourse.

front: Khái niệm 'Vocational Education and Training (VET)' trong Unit 9: Career Paths được định nghĩa như thế nào?
back:
Education focused on practical skills and hands-on preparation for specific trades and technical careers, offering direct pathways into the workforce.

💡 Ví dụ: Many school-leavers choose vocational colleges for culinary arts or automotive mechanics instead of 4-year academic degrees.
🌱 Bản chất: Practical workforce readiness aligned with immediate industrial needs.

front: Phát biểu quy tắc / định lí: 'Object placement with separable phrasal verbs'?
back:
With separable two-part phrasal verbs (take on, fill out), if the object is a pronoun (it, them), it MUST go between verb and particle: fill it out (NOT *fill out it*).

📝 Ví dụ: Here is the application form; please fill it out carefully.
🔑 Ý nghĩa: Rhythmic constraints of English phonology prioritizing weak pronoun stress internally.

front: Phương pháp giải bài toán: 'Replace the underlined phrase with an appropriate phrasal verb: 'She decided to start learning graphic design to improve her job prospects.''?
back:
Các bước giải chi tiết:
Step 1: 'start learning an activity/hobby' translates to phrasal verb 'take up'.
Step 2: Replace: She decided to take up graphic design to improve her job prospects.

👉 Kết luận: take up

front: Bẫy sai lầm cần tránh: Placing pronouns after inseparable or three-part phrasal verbs: *I look forward to meet you*.?
back:
❌ Lỗi sai: Placing pronouns after inseparable or three-part phrasal verbs: *I look forward to meet you*.

💡 Nguyên nhân & Khắc phục: 'To' in 'look forward to' is a preposition, which must be followed by a noun or gerund: look forward to meeting you.
